123 likes, 13 comments - gizmodo on October 30, 2026: "The New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax) is spreading further across the United States and finding new kinds of hosts to burrow itself into.
Several new cases of infestations caused by the parasitic fly have been reported this past week, including the first ever documented in Arizona since the screwworm reemerged in the country earlier this year. New Mexico officials also recently reported the first U.S. case found in a pet cat. October has seen a sizeable increase in reports of the screwworm affecting both domestic and wild animals.

Read more at the link in bio

Story: Ed Cara".

171 likes, 7 comments - gizmodo on October 29, 2026: "According to a report from the Religion News Service, a research administrator at the University of Kentucky successfully received a religious exemption from his employer, excusing him from any expectations to use AI for his work. The man, 45-year-old David Durman, identifies as a humanist and told Religion News Service that he felt being asked to use AI tools like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot, as the University of Kentucky reportedly encouraged its employees to utilize, undermined his belief in the importance of the human parts of life and ran counter to his desire to see human flourishing.

In the letter he submitted to the University of Kentucky’s Office of Equal Opportunity as part of the accommodation request, Durman stated, “Substituting automated machine processing for human presence, authentic listening, and personal responsibility in my work directly conflicts with my obligation to uphold human dignity and flourishing as primary.”

Read more at the link in our bio 📲

Story: AJ Dellinger".

72 likes, 6 comments - gizmodo on October 29, 2026: "The U.S. Federal Trade Commission sent a letter to nine different companies on Wednesday demanding documents related to surveillance pricing, the practice of setting an individualized price for a given customer based on their data.

The companies include Delta, United, JetBlue, Lyft, Uber, DoorDash, Instacart, Target, and Walmart, all of which have been mentioned in news reports in recent years for potentially engaging in some form of surveillance pricing. However, most of the companies have denied the practice, and those caught doing it have insisted it was merely part of a pricing experiment.

Link in our bio to read more 📲

Story: Matt Novak".

36 likes, 3 comments - gizmodo on October 28, 2026: "Yes, Amazon really put a camera in its new screenless Echo Studio speaker. 

The aptly named Echo Studio with Home Camera takes Amazon’s flagship smart speaker and adds a layer of visual intelligence on top. With the new on-device camera, you can ask Alexa about objects in a room (Amazon suggests holding up a board game and asking the speaker how to play it), or use it as a home video feed to surveil your living room (sorry, kids).

Priced at $249 and available to order today. Are you adding this to your household?".
